summary: Find an active-surface potential by bounded bracket expansion and vectorized bisection of a caller-supplied logarithmic charge residual.

identity.relation: root of a caller-supplied logarithmic ion-electron charge residual as a function of potential
identity.direction: reference potential, ion and electron thermal energies, ion charge, active mask, residual evaluator and controls -> potential, final residual, iteration count and convergence flag
identity.definition: For each active surface solve the caller's R(phi)=log(Z*n_i(phi))-log(n_e(phi))=0, represented by logarithmic_charge_residual. Start at phi_ref +/- k*(T_parallel/q + T_e/e), where e=1.602176634e-19 C and k=initial_bracket_thermal. Expand invalid-sign brackets for at most eight rounds, then bisect. Return only when both the maximum active bracket width <= potential_tolerance_v and maximum absolute active midpoint residual <= quasineutral_tolerance within max_iterations. Inactive potentials remain at phi_ref. Finite midpoint evaluation avoids first summing large same-sign endpoints. A strict zero from the caller residual is an exact root hit for the supplied numerical residual and contracts that active bracket to the evaluated point. A small nonzero residual does not trigger this contraction; width and residual tolerances are unchanged.
identity.model: caller-owned decreasing residual with positive values below the root and negative values above it; this operator brackets and bisects but does not calculate either density
identity.geometry: none imposed; broadcast elements represent independent surfaces with one shared vectorized stopping decision
identity.coordinates: caller-supplied axes; NumPy broadcasting does not verify physical surface alignment
identity.boundary: inactive surfaces skip bracketing and stopping checks but their final residual is evaluated; lower endpoint residual must be nonnegative and upper endpoint residual nonpositive after bounded expansion
assumptions: The callback returns a finite, broadcastable, dimensionless logarithmic charge residual for every supplied potential, including inactive positions; the solver cannot validate its electron or ion model.
On active surfaces the residual decreases through the intended root with the specified sign orientation and a root reachable by the bounded expansion.
Both thermal energies are in joules, positive ion charge is in coulombs, and the derived thermal voltage is a bracket scale rather than a physical boundary condition.

inputs.name: potential_reference_v
inputs.description: Reference potential and returned potential on inactive surfaces.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; broadcast with both temperatures and active

inputs.name: temperature_parallel_j
inputs.description: Ion parallel thermal-energy scale for the initial bracket.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: Every converted value finite and strictly positive.

inputs.name: electron_temperature_j
inputs.description: Electron thermal-energy scale for the initial bracket.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: Every converted value finite and strictly positive.

inputs.name: charge_c
inputs.description: Positive ion charge converting parallel thermal energy to volts.
inputs.constraints: Must convert to a finite positive float.

inputs.name: active
inputs.description: Mask selecting surfaces for bracketing and bisection.
inputs.shape: scalar or array; common broadcast shape
inputs.constraints: False positions need no root but are included in final callback evaluation.

inputs.name: residual
inputs.description: Caller-owned evaluator accepting a potential field and returning a Mapping with logarithmic_charge_residual.
inputs.shape: callable result scalar or array broadcastable to common surface shape
inputs.dtype: Python callable returning a Mapping with float64-convertible residual
inputs.constraints: Returned residual must be finite and broadcastable on every evaluation. The callback sees inactive potentials fixed at their references during active bisection.

inputs.name: potential_tolerance_v
inputs.description: Maximum active bracket width at convergence.

inputs.name: quasineutral_tolerance
inputs.description: Maximum absolute active logarithmic residual at convergence.

inputs.name: max_iterations
inputs.description: Maximum number of vectorized midpoint evaluations after bracketing.
inputs.dtype: Python or NumPy integer excluding bool
inputs.constraints: Integer at least 2; float values are not truncated.

inputs.name: initial_bracket_thermal
inputs.description: Multiplier for the sum of ion and electron thermal voltages.

outputs.name: potential_v
outputs.description: Converged active potential and unchanged reference potential at inactive positions.
outputs.shape: common broadcast shape, including scalar shape ()
outputs.constraints: Returned only after all active positions meet both stopping conditions; all-inactive calls skip bisection.

outputs.name: logarithmic_charge_residual
outputs.description: Callback residual evaluated at the complete returned potential field.
outputs.constraints: Finite and broadcastable; inactive values need not meet neutrality tolerance.

outputs.name: iterations
outputs.description: Shared number of vectorized bisection midpoint evaluations.
outputs.constraints: Zero if all positions inactive; otherwise from 1 through max_iterations, not a per-surface count.

outputs.name: converged
outputs.description: Whether all active positions met both stopping conditions or no positions were active.
outputs.constraints: Always True when returned; failures raise instead of returning False.

preconditions: Potential, thermal energies and active mask describe the same surfaces and have broadcast-compatible shapes.
The callback supplies the intended finite decreasing residual with the specified sign orientation and reachable active roots.
supported: One or more active surfaces with one shared stopping decision; mixed active/inactive or all-inactive fields.
excluded: Calculating ion or electron density or verifying the callback's physical model.
Nonmonotone or opposite-sign residuals, roots outside bounded expansion reach, and claims that inactive surfaces are neutral.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError for nonfinite potential or temperatures, nonpositive temperatures or charge, invalid positive controls, max_iterations outside integer >=2, or a callback result without a Mapping containing a finite broadcastable logarithmic_charge_residual. NumPy conversion, a noncallable callback or callback logic may raise TypeError or ValueError; callback exceptions propagate.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Raises RuntimeError if active endpoint signs remain invalid after up to eight expansion rounds. Nonfinite midpoint endpoints raise FloatingPointError; callback validation/errors can also reject an overflowed thermal bracket. Extreme finite thermal scales may still require an unrepresentable bracket.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Raises RuntimeError('ambipolar potential solve did not converge') if both width and residual tolerances are not met on all active surfaces within max_iterations. Adjacent-float stalling is not success: a root between representable potentials that cannot satisfy the residual gate raises rather than widening the tolerance.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No mapping is returned after validation, callback, bracketing or convergence failure; the final callback evaluation can also fail after midpoint stopping.

python.signature: solve_quasineutral_potential(potential_reference_v, temperature_parallel_j, electron_temperature_j, charge_c, active, residual, potential_tolerance_v=1e-08, quasineutral_tolerance=1e-10, max_iterations=100, initial_bracket_thermal=8.0)

example.description: Solve a decreasing residual on one active surface and retain an inactive reference potential.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.closures import solve_quasineutral_potential
e=1.602176634e-19
def residual(phi):
    return {'logarithmic_charge_residual': 0.5-np.asarray(phi)}
r=solve_quasineutral_potential([0.0,17.0],0.1*e,0.1*e,e,[True,False],residual)
np.testing.assert_allclose(r['potential_v'],[0.5,17.0],atol=1e-8)
assert abs(r['logarithmic_charge_residual'][0])<=1e-10
np.testing.assert_allclose(r['logarithmic_charge_residual'][1],-16.5)
assert r['converged'] and 1<=r['iterations']<=100
example.expected: The active potential is about 0.5 V; the inactive potential stays 17 V and retains a nonneutral residual of -16.5.

scope: Direct regressions cover a known-root monotone residual, bracket expansion, active/inactive and all-inactive behavior, and fixed inactive callback potentials.
Selected callback mapping and control failures, failed bracketing, and iteration-budget nonconvergence are asserted.

Exact representable local-neutrality roots at common +/-1e20 and +/-1e308 potentials, plus a manufactured root halfway between adjacent floats that must fail without meeting the original residual tolerance.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Selected manufactured roots, actual local-closure composition, failure paths and finite midpoint cases are supported. An exact zero is a root of the supplied numerical callback, not an independent proof of its physical model; arbitrary models, all floating-point regimes and expert recognition are not established.
known_limitations: The solver cannot detect a numerically valid callback whose residual represents the wrong physics.
Eight expansion rounds and max_iterations do not guarantee a bracket or convergence.
Broadcasting alone does not establish physical coordinate alignment; extreme finite thermal scales may overflow bracket arithmetic.
Public distribution licensing and expert recognition remain pending.
